newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong police practice speedy quashing of riots.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong police practice speedy quashing of riots.

text.p: Hong Kong police firing teargas practised quashing trouble in the streets on Wednesday in case rioting erupts as the handover of the British colony to China appraoches next year.

The practice session was ahead of a public display scheduled for Saturday to demonstrate police ability to put down civil unrest, Stuart McDoull, deputy commandant of the Hong Kong Police Training School, told reporters.
"Of course we hope for a smooth transition...(but) we have to be prepared for every contingency," McDoull said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for over a century and a half, reverts to Chinese rule in 209 days.
Uncertainties and questions hanging over whether freedoms would be preserved have developed into frequent street demonstrations in recent months, but with little violence.
"You have seen a mock riot... you can see how we can respond very quickly to civil unrest," McDoull said.
